description: We are The axis, a 5-person group building a space mission design game for this hackathon. Between us we have experience in game design and coding. We are looking for people to join our team that know godot or 2d-3d modeling.
summary: We developed a game that simulates a space mission. Our game's target audience is people that are new to the magnificent world of space travelling and would like to have an all-encompassing space mission experience while getting familliar with existing spacecrafts and their features. We developed the game because existing tools are usually focused on specific parts of the mission and require advanced knowledge which often becomes an obstacle for aspiring scientists and astronauts. However with our game we've managed to create a simplified version that combines science, knowledge and the most important fun!
details: Our project is a 2D top down game that simulates three types of space missions. First destination is the International Space Station, that is the easiest level, second is the moon, that is the normal level and the third one is the Mars, that is the hardest level. It is built with the engine GODOT, the 3D designs are designed in Blender of the space crafts (Artemis I, Apollo11, Space X dragon crew, Space shuttle and Escapade) and the inside of the space craft are designed by hand on ibis paint drawing app. Lastly the tile maps are designed in Pixelorama. The user through the game learns about the different types of spacecrafts by choosing the right spacecraft for the mission based on the data given by us in the game. Then the user needs to manage their expenses as their upgrade their rocket by buying elements of the spacecraft. If they choose the wrong spacecraft they must start again. The game starts and the player who is inside the spacecraft needs to avoid obstacles that come right at them while collecting additional food in order to survive. This way they practise their coordination skills which are very important for an actual space mission. If they succeed they arrive at their destination where they can collect data and the game ends. We hope to draw new people into the field and provide space enthusiasts with a fun and holistic experience of a space mission since they can use it without needing advanced knowledge. We chose to not use SI because we wanted to boost our creativity and push our limits.
